newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Blast wounds 11 people in Ethiopian town.
newsitem.headline: Blast wounds 11 people in Ethiopian town.

text.p: Eleven people were wounded when an explosion ripped through a bar in an Ethiopian town on Saturday night, state-run television reported on Sunday.
It was not immediately clear whether the explosion was caused by a bomb or a grenade but police said they had launched intensive investigations.
State radio said the bar, located near a railway station in the eastern Ethiopian town of Dire Dawa, was used by travellers.
Three hand grenade attacks hit the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa this month, the last of which was on April 14 when a grenade exploded in a large supermarket, wounding 33 people.
Ethiopian President Meles Zenawi's government blamed Moslem fundamentalists for several bomb attacks last year. Ethiopian authorities remain secretive about their investigations.
British, French and German tourists were wounded last February in a grenade attack on a hotel in the ancient walled city of Harar in the east.
In November, hijackers believed to be Ethiopians seized an Ethiopian Airlines plane and forced it to ditch off the Comoro Islands, killing 125 people on board.

Ethiopian troops, backed by the air force, raided in August alleged Moslem fundamentalist bases in Western Somalia and the al-Ittihad al-Islam (Islamic Unity) party said it would revenge the incursion.
